# @vantreeseba/graphql-mocks

> An npm-workspaces monorepo for the `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks` toolkit: generate realistic, graph-connected mock data from a GraphQL schema using faker, with a companion GraphQL Code Generator plugin for fully typed mock pools.

The runtime introspects every object type in a `GraphQLSchema` (or SDL string) and produces a set of interconnected mock objects where relationships are honored as real object references — `User.todos` references actual mocked `Todo` objects, and `Todo.user` points back to a `User`. Useful for tests, demos, and Storybook mocking. The codegen plugin emits a `SchemaTypeMap` (`{ TypeName: GeneratedType }`) you pass as `TTypes` to `buildMocks` so pools come back typed without a cast.

Key facts:
- TypeScript 5, strict mode, ESM only.
- Two published packages, versioned and released together via semantic-release: `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks` (runtime) and `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks-codegen` (codegen plugin).
- Runtime peer deps: `graphql >=16`, `@faker-js/faker >=9` (plus optional `@graphql-typed-document-node/core >=3` for the Apollo helpers and `@apollo/client >=3.8 <5` for the `./apollo` subpath — the root entry never imports it). Codegen peer deps: `graphql >=16`, `@graphql-codegen/plugin-helpers >=5`, `@graphql-codegen/visitor-plugin-common >=5`.

## API

- `buildMocks(schema, options?)`: Core entry point. Accepts a `GraphQLSchema` or SDL string; returns a `MockResult` keyed by object-type name. Generic `buildMocks<TTypes>(schema)` returns typed pools.
- `MockResult.find(typeName, predicate)`: Find a single mocked item; the item is typed when a `TTypes`/`SchemaTypeMap` is supplied, or `find<T>('Type', …)` for a typed one-off.
- `MockResult.toResolvers()`: Produce Apollo Server / GraphQL Yoga mock resolvers (`{ Type: () => <random item from pool> }`) for `addMocksToSchema`.
- `MockResult.dataForOperation(document, variables?, matchArguments?)`: Execute a query/mutation against the graph and return data shaped to the selection set (lists, fragments, and interface/union fields supported). Return type inferred from a `TypedDocumentNode`.
- `MockResult.toRequestHandler(options?)`: A handler answering any operation from the graph with no registration — memoized per document+variables, with ordered `overrides` (`data`/`errors`/`networkError`/`loading`/`delay`/`once`), a `calls` spy list and `reset()`.
- `mockLink(mocksOrHandler, options?)` from `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks/apollo`: wrap a graph or handler in an `ApolloLink`.
- `mockScenarios(base?, target?)`: the `default` / `loading` / `errored` trio of `MockHandlerOptions`, optionally narrowed to specific operations.
- `MockResult.mockOperationsFrom(module, options?)`: map a codegen document module's export names to lazily built variants.
- `MockResult.ids(type)` / `.at(type, index)` / `.byId(type, id)`: address pooled items directly.
- `paginate(items, args)` / `searchItems(items, term, fields?)`: the array primitives the argument engine uses, exported for wrapper types it cannot reach.
- `mockOperation(query, data, options?)` / `mockOperationVariants(...)`: Build Apollo `MockedProvider` `MockedResponse` entries from supplied result data (`options`: `variables`, `delay`, `error`, `maxUsageCount`). `data` may instead be a `(variables) => data` resolver, producing a `DynamicMockedResponse`.
- `MockResult.mockOperation(query, options?)` / `MockResult.mockOperationVariants(...)`: Same, but resolve the result data from the `MockResult` graph (via `dataForOperation`) so the query's selection set selects the mocks — no data argument needed. Adds `dynamic`, `transform` and a per-call `matchArguments`.
- `BuildMocksOptions`: `count`, `faker`, `seed`, `nullChance`, `scalars`, `overrides`, `relations`, `scenario`, `resolveType`, `addTypename`, `stableIds`, `idPrefix`, `qa`, `listSize`, `matchArguments`.
- `relations` option (`RelationsConfig`): shapes relationship fields after every pool exists — a number, a `{ min, max }` range, `null` (empty), `'all'` (the whole target pool), or `(ctx) => value` picking the related objects from `ctx.pool`. Resolved `[type][field]` → `[type]._default` → `_default` → the flat form, and it reaches root fields through the operation type (`{ Query: { users: 3 } }`). Beats `nullChance` and the QA `lists` profile; `overrides` still beats it. Pools grow to meet demand. Config errors throw (`TypeError` for an unknown/ineligible field or an emptied non-null singular field, `RangeError` for a bad size). `{ _reciprocal: true }` opts into writing each reference back into its inverse field.
- `defineScenarios(map)` / `composeScenarios(...scenarios)`: a scenario is a named partial `BuildMocksOptions` (plus `description`), passed as `scenario: Scenario | Scenario[]` and applied left to right with the explicit options last. Maps merge key by key (`count` per type, `overrides`/`relations` two levels deep, `scalars` by name, `qa` per dimension); everything else is last-wins. `defineScenarios` is an identity function — add `satisfies ScenarioMap<SchemaTypeMap>` for schema-checked keys.
- `buildMatrix(schema, options?)`: crosses a `scenarios` map with `qaPresets` and returns a flat `MatrixCell[]` (`name`, `scenario`, `qa`, `options`, `mocks`). Either axis may be omitted. Each cell gets its own faker seeded from `seed` (`seedPerCell` opts out), and with `stableIds` each cell's ids are prefixed with a slug of its name unless `idPrefix` is set. `buildQaSets` is the QA-only shorthand over the same engine.
- `buildQaSets(schema, options?)`: QA mode. Returns one `{ name, qa, mocks }` set per profile (`QA_PROFILE_NAMES`, or a `profiles` subset), each built from its own seeded faker so a set reproduces independently of the others. Accepts every `BuildMocksOptions` key plus `profiles` and a shared `qa` config the profile merges over.
- `qa` option (`QaProfileName | QaConfig | false`): swaps generators for deliberately out-of-norm values across five dimensions — `text` (`empty`/`whitespace`/`long`/`unicode`/`injection`), `lists` (`empty`/`single`/`huge`, sized by `listSize`, default 100), `nulls` (`none`/`all`/`mixed`), `numbers` (`zero`/`negative`/`boundary`), `dates` (`epoch`/`farPast`/`farFuture`/`mixed`). `scalars` and `overrides` still win; `ID` is left alone; built-in scalars stay serializable but custom scalar constraints are not respected.
- `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks-codegen` plugin: emits `export type SchemaTypeMap = { … }` for every object type (root operation and introspection types excluded, entries sorted).

## Examples

- Basic: `const mocks = buildMocks(schema); mocks.User; mocks.Todo;` — 5 of each, with `todo.user` pointing into `mocks.User`.
- Deterministic + per-type counts: `buildMocks(schema, { seed: 42, count: { User: 10, Todo: 50, _default: 5 }, nullChance: 0.1 })`.
- Custom scalar mockers: `buildMocks(schema, { scalars: { DateTime: (f) => f.date.recent().toISOString(), CityName: (f) => f.location.city() } })`.
- Field overrides (receive the seeded faker and `{ index, typeName, fieldName }`): `buildMocks(schema, { overrides: { User: { name: () => 'Alice', loginCount: (f, { index }) => index === 0 ? 0 : f.number.int(500) } } })`.
- Stable ids: `buildMocks(schema, { stableIds: true }).User[0]` → `{ __typename: 'User', id: 'User-0', … }`.
- Interfaces/unions: `buildMocks(schema, { resolveType: (name) => name === 'SearchResult' ? 'Post' : 'User' })`.
- Typed pools: `buildMocks<{ User: User; Todo: Todo }>(schema)` or `buildMocks<SchemaTypeMap>(schema)`.
- Operation data: `const data = mocks.dataForOperation(UserByIdQuery)` → `{ user: { …selected fields, nested via wired refs… } }`.
- Apollo MockedProvider (data from the graph): `<MockedProvider mocks={[mocks.mockOperation(AwardByIdQuery)]} />`.
- QA mode, single profile: `buildMocks(schema, { seed: 42, qa: 'longText' })` or tuned: `buildMocks(schema, { qa: { text: 'unicode', lists: 'huge', nulls: 'mixed' } })`.
- QA sets for Storybook/Apollo: `buildQaSets(schema, { seed: 42 }).map((set) => ({ name: set.name, parameters: { apolloClient: { mocks: [set.mocks.mockOperation(UsersQuery)] } } }))`.
- Relationship shaping: `buildMocks(schema, { relations: { User: { todos: 0, posts: { min: 1, max: 2 } }, Post: { comments: 'all', author: ({ pool }) => pool[0] }, Query: { users: 3 } } })`.
- Named scenarios: `const scenarios = defineScenarios({ newUser: { count: { User: 1 }, relations: { User: { todos: null } }, overrides: { User: { loginCount: () => 0 } } } }); buildMocks(schema, { scenario: scenarios.newUser, seed: 42 })`.
- Scenario × QA matrix: `buildMatrix(schema, { scenarios, qaPresets: [false, 'longText', 'hugeLists'], seed: 42 })` → one cell per combination, named `"newUser × longText"`.
- Argument matching (opt-in): `buildMocks(schema, { matchArguments: true })` — `user(id: "User-2")`, `users(skip: 10, limit: 5)` and `posts(titleContains: "x")` select data; unmatched lists return `[]`, unmatched singulars fall back to a random pick, and auto-filled variables are ignored.
- Any-operation transport: `new ApolloClient({ cache, link: mockLink(mocks) })`, or `await mocks.toRequestHandler()({ query, variables })`.
- Story states: `const s = mockScenarios({}, 'UserById'); mocks.toRequestHandler(s.loading)`.
